title:
BEFORE
THE FIRST
PLATE
dek: A short note on what this atlas is, what it will not do, and how to move through it.

blocks.head: Russian death is not **one thing.**
paras: The title names a field of evidence, not a national character. What survives is a set of documents about particular places and times: a village recorded by a folklorist, a parish regulated by a synod, a cemetery administered by a city, a memorial built by a state.
These documents overlap and they disagree. The atlas keeps the disagreement on the page instead of averaging it into a custom.
blocks.tr: Printed Slavonic text on a Last Judgment icon — writing in an image, not a lament

blocks.head: A coffin, a cloth, a bowl of grain, **a stone.**
paras: The plates treat things as documents: what they were made of, who handled them, what they were for and who wrote about them. A photograph is a record of someone’s decision to photograph as much as it is a record of a grave.
Every image carries its credit and its licence. Every image also carries a button that shows the file as it was before the atlas touched it: the damage you see is ours, and it is declared.

blocks.head: Where the evidence stops, **the sheet stays empty.**
paras: Plate L is almost white on purpose. It lists what is missing — a field survey of a provincial cemetery, a municipal burial register, a scholarly account of post-Soviet digital memorials — and draws the gap instead of filling it.
Nothing here is invented to close a hole: no quotations, no archive numbers, no photographs staged as history. One photograph from Ukraine appears once, and is labelled as Ukrainian.

items.head: In a line
items.text: Plates A to L, from the room where a death occurs to the archive that cannot hold it.

items.head: In a net
items.text: The index crosses plates with objects, concepts and places; the words page lists the vocabulary.

items.head: On the ground
items.text: The map and the chronology pin each claim to a place or a date — or refuse to.

closing: The aesthetic is not darkness. **It is Russian death, remembered through matter.**
